item.title: Theoretical Contributions to Advance the Business and Society Debate
item.content:encoded:
Jay Joseph, American University of Beirut

Harry Van Buren III, University of Tennessee at Chattanooga

Jennifer Oetzel, American University

Angelika Rettberg, Universidad de los Andes

Global peace is needed now more than ever, yet "peace" still fails to feature in mainstream business and society debates. For over 20 years, "business and peace" has led this debate in business and management studies. Business and peace has generated a broad array of research studies that link business activity to peacebuilding; however, the high volume of descriptive, case-based, and practice-based research in the field, combined with the growing number of parallel contributions to conflict and peace-related topics in general management studies, presents challenges for moving a coherent debate on peace and business forward.

Appel publié par Business & Society. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Stakeholder-based theories associated with business and peace
  • Systems perspectives on business and peace
  • Intergroup and contact theories in business contexts
  • Business and human rights frameworks
  • Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and political CSR
  • Governance processes in business and peace
  • Organizing processes and organization studies
  • Normative and ethical frameworks addressing corruption and corporate misconduct
  • International business frameworks in conflict settings
  • Entrepreneurship and entrepreneurial models for conflict-resolution and peace
  • Advanced conceptual development for conflict and peace research
  • Boundary work to clarify field domains in business and peace
  • Theoretical consolidation and advancement of business and peace foundations
